topology.cycle_note: Triangle confirmed on the annotated sketch: bathroom_2 carries two doors, one to the Living room and one to the Hall. hall - living_room - bathroom_2 - hall is the property's only cycle and the only place a stitch can be caught contradicting itself.
topology.archway_note: Every Hall connection is an open archway. At the photo tier this is the best possible case: an archway carries a through-view, so every adjacency in the property has direct image evidence and none has to be guessed. A property behind closed doors would leave most edges structurally invisible at this tier.
topology.benchmark_gap: The flip side is that the benchmark now contains no closed-door adjacency at all, so the photo tier's worst failure mode goes unmeasured. Staging one - close the Living room's wall D door, or hang a sheet over an archway, and re-capture - would cost one extra capture and turn an unmeasured weakness into a reported interval.
topology.unassigned_note: Three Hall openings have no named destination and three bedrooms have no named opening. The pairing is near-certain but is not stated, and adjacency is scored.

open_questions: Tape uncertainty: one wall and one opening measured three times. The last thing standing between this benchmark and a quotable interval.

layout_from_sketch.note: Wall A's four archways map onto the four rooms in the east column, in order. That is what confirms arch_a3 and arch_a4 as the two eastern bedrooms rather than leaving them unassigned.
